data.title: Halobetasol propionate (0.05% / 0.01% lotion)
data.summary: IV Topical corticosteroids · Super-potent fluorinated steroid (US class 1); 0.01% lotion in a newer vehicle remains high/super-high potency
data.body:
_Topicals · IV Topical corticosteroids_

**Class:** Super-potent fluorinated steroid (US class 1); 0.01% lotion in a newer vehicle remains high/super-high potency

## Mechanism of action
- Glucocorticoid receptor agonist with very high potency (similar to clobetasol)
- The 0.01% lotion (polymeric emulsion) delivers drug efficiently, allowing a lower concentration with less HPA suppression and longer use (up to 8 weeks)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Plaque psoriasis (adults)
- Other steroid-responsive thick dermatoses (lichen simplex, hypertrophic lichen planus)

## Dose & formulations
- 0.05% cream/ointment: once or twice daily, max 50 g/week, up to 2 weeks
- 0.01% lotion: once daily for up to 8 weeks, max 50 g/week
- Halobetasol 0.01% + tazarotene 0.045% lotion is also available for psoriasis

## Adverse effects
- As for super-potent steroids: atrophy, striae, folliculitis, HPA suppression

## Contraindications
- Face, flexures, groin; children under 12–18 (label); untreated infection, rosacea

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid large areas.

## Viva points
- Class 1 steroid; 0.01% lotion allows 8-week use
- Fixed combination with tazarotene reduces retinoid irritation and steroid atrophy

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.45; product information for 0.01% lotion (Bryhali). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
